title: The version delta closes — contracts and pipelineResult converge
description: PGE's sprint_exit writes version: attempts; the imperative runSprintCycle writes none. Close the last contract delta, which closes pipelineResult with it since that field is a container for the same objects.

successCriteria.description: Both engines agree on `version` for an equivalent run — by giving the imperative engine an equivalent monotone, replay-stable source, not by deleting the field the rank-aware channel join reads.
The value stays replay-stable: two runs over the same input produce the same version, proven by execution.
Neither 'contracts' nor 'pipelineResult' appears in the divergence set, verified by running the harness.
VOLATILE_KEYS is unchanged — convergence is real, not achieved by excluding the field from comparison.
Golden cases whose artifacts move are re-captured in this sprint, diff hunks read.
Full suite, typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build green, and the golden gate passing at or above its replay floor.

stopConditions: The imperative engine has no replay-stable monotone source at its settle site — report what IS available rather than shipping something a replay cannot reproduce.
definitionOfDone: All required criteria met, the full suite plus typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build green, the golden gate passing, and every documentation claim added backed by a test that fails when the claim stops being true.
generatorNotes: PGE derives version from `attempts` — a count-filter over the appendById evaluations channel, order-invariant by construction (src/pge/nodes/sprint-review.ts:215). The imperative engine tracks its own iteration count in runSprintCycle; use that, and check it increments across the same transitions. Sprint 3 of spec-20260812-terminal-vocabulary documents why a wall-clock or ordering-derived value is disqualified. Do NOT give the schema a .default() — it would stamp the seeded copy and break the channel join. Run the suite as `npx vitest run --exclude '**/.claude/worktrees/**' --exclude '**/node_modules/**'` — a bare run picks up nested worktrees. Verify on a CLEAN checkout, not just the working tree: this repo has twice been green locally and red in CI because uncommitted state was carrying the result.
evaluatorNotes: Run the same input twice and diff the version. Then confirm VOLATILE_KEYS did not grow — that is the cheap way this criterion could be faked. Finally verify pipelineResult closed as a CONSEQUENCE of contracts rather than being separately special-cased.
